More than 1,300 people are missing in Nepal and Tibet, including 47 Americans, after a glacial collapse caused catastrophic floods, with video showing mud sweeping through entire communities. Drone footage in Nepal showed roads destroyed and buildings buried by thundering water the color of wet cement. Nepalese authorities ramped up operations in the worst-affected districts of Nuwakot and Rasuwa. The disaster in Nepal and Tibet is not a one-off. The Lhende Khola river system has now flooded twice in just 14 months and the increasingly unstable Himalayan ice system threatens communities, infrastructure and water supplies across one of the world’s most densely populated regions. The region saw similar flash floods in August last year, when a glacial lake in Tibet overflowed because of high temperatures. Nine people were killed, and critical infrastructure, including a bridge connecting Nepal and China, was damaged.

A day in Kathmandu 📿🇳🇵 The city where the sacred peaks of the Himalayas meet the pulse of ancient civilization,Kathmandu is the spiritual heart of Nepal, a city where Hinduism and Buddhism coexist in every temple, ritual, and prayer flag. Prayer wheels spin beside burning incense, golden stupas rise above medieval rooftops and centuries-old traditions still shape daily life. Before trekking into the mountains, spend a few days exploring this vibrant, chaotic, and deeply sacred capital. 📿Spiritual Highlights: One of the most iconic spots to visit is the Boudhanath Stupa, one of the holiest sites in Tibetan Buddhism, where monks chant and incense swirls through the air. Witness the powerful energy of Pashupatinath Temple, Nepal’s most sacred Hindu shrine, perched on the banks of the Bagmati River. And climb to Swayambhunath (the Monkey Temple), a 2,000-year-old hilltop stupa where Buddhist and Hindu elements blend seamlessly along with sweeping views over the valley. 🛕 Ancient Cities: Wander the timeworn alleys of Bhaktapur and Patan, where every brick and temple tells a story. These ancient cities are living museums, home to UNESCO-listed durbar squares, ornate palaces, and the intricate woodwork of the Newar artisans. Don’t miss the Patan Museum — a quiet gem showcasing Nepal’s spiritual art and history. 🏙️Markets & City Life: Get lost in the colors and chaos of Thamel, the city’s backpacker hub filled with trekking shops, rooftop cafés, and buzzing streets. For a more local vibe, explore Ason Bazaar, one of the oldest markets in the city, where locals haggle over spices, grains, and textiles. Refuel with a plate of steaming momo or a glass of fresh lassi from a street stall.
